title: A Honest Appraisal of 'The Help' (LONG POST)

commenti.body:
You mentioned Spike Lee, who made tremendously powerful statements in Bamboozled, one of which was: Whites drew a portrait that looks at a culture in every wrong way on purpose. 

The image of blacks in America was tragically exaggerated during and after the slave trade thanks to white fear mongering. Movies like The Help, directed by a white man, based on a book written by a white woman are a direct product of that mindset. No matter how forward thinking a white person believes they are, every idea they have of black culture is based on white amplification of the wrong understanding. A perception that was the springboard for f\*cked up messages. I don't have time for a longer reply, but let me sum up by saying the series Them (season 1) had SO much to say about this, but nothing sticks in my brain quite like the white woman, terrified of the new black neighbors across the street, getting abducted by a white serial killer because she was raised in an environment that led her down a bad f\*cking path: believing white was right, when in actuality white people's misaligned depiction of a non-white culture was crafted solely so whites could remain the dominant race. This caused the women to see safety in every white corner of the world and darkness in everyone that didn't look like her. She couldn't have been more deceived.
